HARD NEGATIVE -- the only kind that moves fp_rate. Every other negative here is a BUSCO ortholog, conserved by definition and therefore easy. This gene is ancient but LOOKS novel to the pipeline: it hits all 6 outgroup proteomes at 3.1e-116..4.9e-87, yet its in-genome paralog NCU03312 (UniProt Q7SEN2) wins every head-to-head, so the pre-2026-09-20 paralog-competition filter erased all 6 cells and called it a lineage-specific novelty. Issue #128 / PR #136 added the 1e-20 rescue floor; this control guards that fix. CONFIDENCE: the tree places ALR1/ALR2_YEAST as sister to the A7UWR3 ingroup clade, which is good evidence the outgroup orthologs are real -- but this is our own phylogeny, not an independently published result. Treat as strong-but-unconfirmed until someone checks it. Its 4 ingroup siblings (Afum Q4WTR5, Cimm J3K7R2, Ztri F9XHY1, Amega A0ACF5C4E7) were ALREADY called correctly by the old pipeline, so adding them too would catch an over-correction in the other direction -- they still need the same UniProt->FungiDB ID translation before they can be used here.
